final answer
COGS is booked once because only one of the two documents posts stock entries for a given item. A Sales Invoice linked to a Delivery Note has `update_stock = 0`, so it posts no stock or COGS entries of its own. I read the Delivery Note and Sales Invoice code. I did not open `sales_order.py` and am only recalling its function names. The `get_gl_entries` call into `BaseStockGLComposer` and the `validate_delivery_note` and `validate_multiple_billing` internals were also not read. **1. Sales Order** (`selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`) - The Sales Order posts no stock or GL entries. It reserves stock (Bin reserved qty, `Stock Reservation Entry`) and tracks `delivered_qty` and `billed_amt`. - `make_delivery_note` and `make_sales_invoice` are the mapped-doc creators. They copy `so_detail` and `against_sales_order` into the child rows. - Those links drive later status updates. `update_prevdoc_status` updates delivered qty, and the billing-status updates handle billed amount. **2. Delivery Note** (`stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`, class `DeliveryNote`) - `on_submit` runs these steps in order: - `update_prevdoc_status` updates delivered qty on the Sales Order. - `update_billing_status` calls `BillingStatusService` in `stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/billing_status.py`. - `update_stock_reservation_entries` updates reservations. - `update_stock_ledger` creates the Stock Ledger Entries. Its implementation is in `controllers/selling_controller.py` (`SellingController.update_stock_ledger`). - `make_gl_entries` posts the GL entries. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle` reposts later entries. - `get_gl_entries` delegates to `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` (`stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`). That class extends `BaseStockGLComposer` and posts Dr COGS / Cr Inventory at valuation rate. - `validate_expense_account` sets each stock item's `expense_account` to the company's "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" (SDBNB) account. This happens when `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` is on and the item has no `against_sales_invoice`. Otherwise it uses the default expense account. - So with SDBNB enabled, the Delivery Note books Dr SDBNB / Cr Stock. SDBNB acts as a temporary COGS holding account. **3. Sales Invoice** (`accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`, class `SalesInvoice`) - When created from a Delivery Note, `update_stock = 0`. The `update_stock_ledger` calls in `on_submit` and `on_cancel` are guarded by `if self.update_stock == 1`. - `validate_delivery_note` and `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", "amount")` stop the invoice from over-billing a delivery. - `make_gl_entries` calls `get_gl_entries`, which delegates to `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose` (`accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`). That produces: - `make_customer_gl_entry` for Dr Receivable. - `make_tax_gl_entries` and `make_item_gl_entries` for Cr Income and tax. - `make_item_gl_entries` adds the stock/COGS entries (`super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()`) only if `update_stock` is set and perpetual inventory is on. In the Delivery Note flow that branch is skipped, so no second COGS posting. - `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` reclassifies the SDBNB amount. - `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` returns immediately if `update_stock` is set or perpetual inventory is off. Otherwise, for each item, `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` finds the Delivery Note's valuation as follows: - It requires a `delivery_note` or `dn_detail` on the row and a stock item. - It reads the Delivery Note Item's `expense_account` and checks it is an SDBNB-type account that differs from the invoice item's expense account (`_is_sdbnb_reversal`). - It reads `stock_value_difference / actual_qty` from the Delivery Note's Stock Ledger Entry for that `voucher_detail_no`. - It multiplies that rate by `item.stock_qty`. - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` then posts Cr SDBNB / Dr the item's real COGS expense account for that amount. - After submit, the invoice updates `billed_amt` on the Sales Order and Delivery Note via `update_billed_amount_in_delivery_note` and `update_billed_amount_based_on_so`. This keeps the Delivery Note's `per_billed` status current. **Net result** - The Delivery Note posts the only stock entry. The Sales Invoice posts no Stock Ledger Entry, only a GL reclassification. - With SDBNB enabled, the Delivery Note books Dr SDBNB / Cr Stock. The invoice later moves the same valuation from SDBNB to COGS. - With SDBNB disabled, the Delivery Note books COGS directly and the invoice books nothing for stock. - In both cases the stock leaves inventory once and COGS is recognised once. - If the invoice is created without a Delivery Note and `update_stock` is checked, the invoice posts the stock and COGS entries itself.

final answer
**Short answer:** ERPNext books COGS from the Stock Ledger Entries (SLEs) of whichever document moves the stock. The Sales Invoice moves stock only when `update_stock=1`, and validation forbids that on any invoice linked to a Delivery Note. So each item's COGS is posted once, by the Delivery Note, unless the invoice itself ships the goods. I read the code paths below but did not run any of it. **1. Sales Order** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py` and `mapper.py`) - A Sales Order posts no stock or GL entries. - It only tracks progress. `update_prevdoc_status` and the Delivery Note's and Sales Invoice's `status_updater` configurations update `delivered_qty` and `per_delivered` on the Sales Order. - `mapper.make_sales_invoice` creates an invoice from the order. `stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py::make_sales_invoice` creates one from a Delivery Note and sets `dn_detail` and `delivery_note` on each item row. It also excludes quantities already invoiced or returned. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`) - `DeliveryNote.on_submit` writes the SLEs, which move the stock out of the warehouse. - `get_gl_entries` calls `DeliveryNoteGLComposer`, in `delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`. That class extends `BaseStockGLComposer` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`). - `BaseStockGLComposer.compose` loops over the SLEs and posts a debit to the Expense account for the item (COGS) and a credit to the Stock-in-Hand account at `stock_value_difference`. This is the one place COGS is booked. - `validate_expense_account` sets `item.expense_account` to the company's "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" (SDBNB) account when `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` is on. In that case the Delivery Note's debit goes to SDBNB (a liability-type holding account) instead of COGS. - `update_billing_status` keeps `per_billed` on the Delivery Note current. **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py` and `services/gl_composer.py`) - `validate_delivery_note` raises an error when `update_stock` is set and any item has a `delivery_note`: "Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes". An invoice linked to a Delivery Note therefore never creates its own SLEs. - `on_submit` runs `update_stock_ledger` only when `update_stock == 1`, and then runs `make_gl_entries`. - `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose` always posts the customer, tax and income entries. - `make_item_gl_entries` adds the stock and COGS entries only when `update_stock` is on and perpetual inventory is enabled. In that case it calls `super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()`, which is the stock controller's SLE-based COGS posting. - For an invoice billed from a Delivery Note, `update_stock` is 0, so no COGS or inventory entries are made at invoice time. - `update_billing_status_in_dn` updates `billed_amt` and `per_billed` on the Delivery Note. **Reversing SDBNB when the invoice is submitted** (only if SDBNB is enabled) - `compose` calls `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries`. It returns early if `update_stock` is set or perpetual inventory is off. - For each item, `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` reads the Delivery Note's SLE (via `dn_detail`). It takes `valuation_rate = stock_value_difference / actual_qty` and multiplies that by the invoice row's `stock_qty`. - `_is_sdbnb_reversal` confirms that the Delivery Note's expense account is of type "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" and differs from the item's COGS account. - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` then credits SDBNB and debits the item's COGS account, so COGS is recognised at invoice time on the Delivery Note's valuation. - The net effect is that stock is reduced once (Delivery Note SLE), and COGS reaches the P&L once. With SDBNB off, the Delivery Note posts it directly. With SDBNB on, the Delivery Note parks the amount in SDBNB and the invoice moves it to COGS. **Supporting pieces** - Quantity guards: `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", ...)` stops over-billing a Delivery Note. - Reposting: `repost_item_valuation._update_post_delivery_billed_vouchers` reposts invoices created after a Delivery Note, so the SDBNB reversal stays in line with the Delivery Note's revalued amounts.

final answer
**Short answer:** the Delivery Note books the stock movement and the cost entry, and the Sales Invoice books only the revenue. The one exception is that, with the optional "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" account, the invoice reclassifies the cost. It never books it a second time. I read this from the code. I did not run any scenario. ## 1. Sales Order The files are `selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`, `mapper.py` and `services/status.py`. The class is `SalesOrder(SellingController)`. - `on_submit` calls `update_prevdoc_status`, `check_credit_limit`, `update_reserved_qty` and `create_stock_reservation_entries`. It writes no stock ledger entries and no GL entries. - `update_reserved_qty` is implemented in `services/reservation.py`. It only reserves quantity in the Bin. - `mapper.make_delivery_note` and `mapper.make_sales_invoice` create the downstream documents. They carry `so_detail` and `against_sales_order` forward on each item row. - `update_delivery_status` and `update_picking_status` in `services/status.py` track the percentage delivered. ## 2. Delivery Note The file is `stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`. The class is `DeliveryNote(SellingController)`. `SellingController` is in `controllers/selling_controller.py` and extends `StockController`, which is in `controllers/stock_controller.py`. - `on_submit` calls `update_prevdoc_status`, which updates `delivered_qty` and `per_delivered` on the Sales Order. - It then calls `update_billing_status`, which delegates to `BillingStatusService` in `delivery_note/services/billing_status.py`. - It then calls `update_stock_ledger`, which is `SellingController.update_stock_ledger` (around line 676). That writes the Stock Ledger Entries at the valuation rate. - Finally it calls `make_gl_entries`, which is `StockController.make_gl_entries` and `get_gl_entries`. - With perpetual inventory enabled, the GL entries are Dr COGS and Cr Stock in Hand. - `validate_expense_account` (around line 438) handles the optional SDBNB setup. If the company has `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` set, items on a Delivery Note get `expense_account = stock_delivered_but_not_billed`. The debit then goes to that interim account instead of COGS. - `on_cancel` reverses the stock ledger entries and GL entries through `make_gl_entries_on_cancel`. ## 3. Sales Invoice The files are `accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py` and `services/gl_composer.py`. The class is `SalesInvoice(SellingController)`. - **Billing quantities:** - `validate_delivery_note` checks that any linked Delivery Note is submitted. - `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", ...)` stops a Delivery Note row being over-billed. - After submit, `update_billing_status_in_dn` (around line 1085 onward) updates `billed_amt` and `per_billed` on the Delivery Note. For rows with no `dn_detail` it calls `update_billed_amount_based_on_so` instead. - **The key flag is `update_stock`.** The invoice writes stock ledger entries only if `update_stock == 1`, in `on_submit` and `on_cancel` (lines 443–460 and 534–542). - When you map a Delivery Note into an invoice, `update_stock` is 0. - Without it, `SalesInvoice.make_gl_entries` and `get_gl_entries` produce only receivable, income and tax entries (the revenue side). They produce no COGS and no stock entries. - `StockController.get_gl_entries` is not the source of any COGS from the invoice in this path. - `validate_delivery_note` and the `dn_required` check keep the user from combining `update_stock` with a Delivery Note reference. If both applied, stock would move twice. - **The SDBNB reversal:** `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` in `gl_composer.py` (lines 164–253) handles the accounting. - It returns immediately if `doc.update_stock` is set or perpetual inventory is off. - `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` applies only to stock items with a `delivery_note` or `dn_detail`. - It reads the original Delivery Note's Stock Ledger Entry through `voucher_no`, `voucher_detail_no` and `is_cancelled=0`. The valuation per unit is `stock_value_difference / actual_qty`, and the amount is that rate times `item.stock_qty`. - `_is_sdbnb_reversal` confirms the Delivery Note account has type "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" and differs from the item's expense account. - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` then posts Cr SDBNB and Dr the real COGS account. - The amount comes from the Delivery Note's own ledger entry. It is not recalculated at the invoice's date, so the reclassification matches what the Delivery Note booked. ## How COGS is booked exactly once - **Without SDBNB:** the Delivery Note posts Dr COGS and Cr Stock when it is submitted. The invoice has `update_stock = 0`, so it posts nothing for stock or COGS. COGS is booked once, at delivery. - **With SDBNB:** the Delivery Note posts Dr SDBNB and Cr Stock. The invoice then posts Dr COGS and Cr SDBNB for the same amount. The SDBNB account nets to zero and COGS is recognised once, at billing. - **Direct invoicing with no Delivery Note:** when you tick `update_stock`, the invoice does its own stock ledger entries and COGS through `StockController.get_gl_entries`. No Delivery Note exists in that case, so nothing is duplicated. - **Cancellation:** `make_gl_entries_on_cancel` and `update_stock_ledger` on cancel reverse the entries for each document separately.

I traced the three doctypes and I'm now writing up the answer. I haven't read `DeliveryNoteGLComposer`'s body or the `StockController` composer it inherits from, so the Delivery Note cost-booking details below come from the call sites and the Sales Invoice side. ## Lifecycle **1. Sales Order** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/`) - A Sales Order books no stock movement and no GL entries. It only reserves and tracks quantities. - `mapper.make_delivery_note` (`sales_order/mapper.py:232`) turns a submitted Sales Order into a Delivery Note. - The `condition()` helper only maps rows where `delivered_qty < qty`. - `update_item()` sets the Delivery Note qty to `qty - delivered_qty`. - `field_map` links each row with `so_detail` (the Sales Order Item name) and `against_sales_order`. - `mapper.make_sales_invoice` in the same file is the direct Sales Order → Sales Invoice path. - `SalesOrder.update_prevdoc_status` (`sales_order.py:435`) and the `status_updater` machinery keep `delivered_qty`, `billed_amt` and `per_delivered` up to date. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`) - `DeliveryNote.on_submit` (line 481) runs these steps in order: - `update_prevdoc_status()` updates the Sales Order's delivered qty. - `update_billing_status()` goes through `BillingStatusService` in `services/billing_status.py`. - `update_stock_ledger()` posts the stock ledger entries (SLEs). - `make_gl_entries()` posts the accounting entries. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle()` reposts later entries affected by the change. - `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries` (line 433) delegates to `DeliveryNoteGLComposer.compose` in `delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`. It posts Dr COGS / Cr Stock at the valuation rate from the SLE. - `DeliveryNote.validate_expense_account` (line 438) is the first half of the "book once" design. - When the company has `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` and a `stock_delivered_but_not_billed` (SDBNB) account, it sets each stock item's `expense_account` to the SDBNB account. - So the Delivery Note debits the SDBNB account instead of the real COGS account. - It throws if a Delivery Note row linked to a Sales Invoice (`against_sales_invoice`) uses SDBNB. - `delivery_note/mapper.py` has `make_sales_invoice` (line 62). - It maps the Delivery Note row name to `dn_detail` (line 141) and the Delivery Note name to `delivery_note` (line 142). - `get_invoiced_qty_map` and `get_returned_qty_map` stop the same quantity from being invoiced twice. - Sales Invoice items mapped from a Delivery Note keep `update_stock = 0`. **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`) - `SalesInvoice.on_submit` (line 421) runs these steps: - `update_prevdoc_status()` and `update_billing_status_in_dn()` update billing on the Sales Order and Delivery Note. - `update_stock_ledger()` runs **only if `update_stock == 1`** (line 443). - `make_gl_entries()` posts the accounting entries. - `SalesInvoice.get_gl_entries` (line 1070) delegates to `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose` in `sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`. That covers the receivable, income, taxes and discounts, plus the SDBNB reversal described below. ## How cost of goods sold is booked exactly once There are two separate guards. 1. **Stock moves once.** - The Delivery Note posts the SLE. - A Sales Invoice created from a Delivery Note has `update_stock = 0`, so it never calls `update_stock_ledger`. - Stock is only deducted by a Sales Invoice when `update_stock = 1`, which is the case where there is no Delivery Note. - `DeliveryNote` `status_updater` conditions (around lines 175 and 219) explicitly exclude Sales Invoice Items whose parent has `update_stock = 1`. A Sales Invoice that moves stock itself therefore doesn't count as billing a Delivery Note. 2. **The cost entry is moved, not repeated (SDBNB reversal).** - `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` (`gl_composer.py:164`) returns immediately if `doc.update_stock` is set or perpetual inventory is off. - Otherwise, for each item it calls `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item`: - It requires `item.delivery_note` or `item.dn_detail`, and a stock item. - It reads the Delivery Note Item's `expense_account` and calls `_is_sdbnb_reversal`. That is true only if the account type is "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" and it differs from the invoice item's `expense_account`. - It reads the Delivery Note's actual SLE (`voucher_no`, `voucher_detail_no = dn_detail`, `is_cancelled = 0`). It computes `valuation_rate = stock_value_difference / actual_qty` and multiplies by the invoiced `item.stock_qty`. - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` (line 222) then posts: - Cr SDBNB account, for the valuation amount. - Dr the item's real expense (COGS) account, for the same amount. The net effect: - **Delivery Note:** Dr SDBNB / Cr Stock, which is an interim liability-like account. - **Sales Invoice:** Dr COGS / Cr SDBNB, which clears the interim account and recognises the expense. - **Result:** COGS is recognised once, at the invoice, and only for the quantity actually invoiced. Partial billing works because the amount is proportional to `item.stock_qty`. - **Cost basis:** the Delivery Note's own SLE valuation is the source of the amount. The invoice never recomputes it from current stock. If SDBNB isn't enabled, the Delivery Note itself debits COGS. The invoice then finds no SDBNB account on the Delivery Note Item, so `_is_sdbnb_reversal` is false and it posts no cost entries. Either way COGS is booked once. Cancellation and returns are handled through `on_cancel` and the reversing GL paths (`make_gl_entries_on_cancel`, `make_reverse_gl_entries`). Returns can auto-issue a credit note through `BillingStatusService.make_return_invoice`.

**Short answer:** COGS is booked once, by whichever document moves the stock. A Sales Invoice that bills a Delivery Note never moves stock and never books COGS. Optionally, the Delivery Note parks its cost in a "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" (SDBNB) account, and the invoice reverses that into COGS. I read the Sales Invoice and Delivery Note code below. I did not open the Sales Order controller itself, only its mapper and the status-updater configs. The `get_item_details.py` lines and the base `get_gl_entries` are inferred from search hits and the call sites, not read in full. **1. Sales Order** (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/`) - The Sales Order has no stock or GL effect. It only tracks `delivered_qty`, `per_delivered`, `billed_amt` and `per_billed`. - `mapper.py::make_sales_invoice` creates the invoice. It sets `so_detail` on each invoice item and subtracts already-billed quantity (`get_billed_qty`). - Delivery Note creation from the order sets `so_detail` and `against_sales_order`, which is how the Delivery Note links back to the order. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`) - `DeliveryNote.__init__` builds `status_updater`. It updates `Sales Order Item.delivered_qty`, `per_delivered` and `delivery_status`, and `Sales Invoice Item.delivered_qty` through `si_detail`. It also updates the Pick List. - On submit, the stock ledger entries (Stock Ledger Entry rows) are created and `get_gl_entries` is called. - `get_gl_entries` delegates to `services/gl_composer.py::DeliveryNoteGLComposer.compose`, which inherits `BaseStockGLComposer`. This is where COGS is booked: Dr the item's expense account, Cr the inventory account, at valuation. This only happens when `is_perpetual_inventory_enabled(company)` is true (`erpnext/__init__.py`). - If the company has `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` set, the item's expense account on the Delivery Note defaults to the SDBNB account. That default comes from `stock/get_item_details.py`, around lines 455–472. - The Delivery Note validation around lines 443–460 of `delivery_note.py` rejects the SDBNB account on items that are already linked to a Sales Invoice. That avoids a second booking. - `services/billing_status.py` and `mapper.py` track `per_billed`. They use `Sales Invoice Item.dn_detail` and `delivery_note`, so the same quantity cannot be billed twice. **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/`) - `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note` throws "Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes" if `update_stock` is on and any item has a `delivery_note`. This is the guard that prevents a second stock movement. - `update_status_updater_args` only adds the stock status updaters when `update_stock` is 1. A Delivery Note-based invoice therefore does not touch `delivered_qty` itself. - In `services/gl_composer.py::SalesInvoiceGLComposer`: - `compose` always books receivable, tax and income through `make_customer_gl_entry`, `make_tax_gl_entries` and `make_item_gl_entries`. - `make_item_gl_entries` adds the stock and COGS rows only when `cint(doc.update_stock)` is set and perpetual inventory is on. In that case it calls `super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()`, the base stock GL logic that books COGS from the invoice's own stock ledger entries. A Delivery Note-based invoice has `update_stock=0`, so no COGS rows come from here. - `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries` returns immediately if `doc.update_stock` is set or perpetual inventory is off. Otherwise it loops over the items. - `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` finds the original Delivery Note's stock ledger entry through `delivery_note` and `dn_detail`. It computes `valuation_rate × item.stock_qty`, so a partial invoice reverses only its own quantity. - `_is_sdbnb_reversal` checks that the Delivery Note's expense account has account type "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" and differs from the item's expense account. - `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries` then posts Cr SDBNB and Dr the item's COGS account. - `repost_item_valuation.py::_update_post_delivery_billed_vouchers` reposts the linked invoices when a Delivery Note's valuation changes. This keeps the SDBNB reversal matching the Delivery Note's entries. **How COGS is booked exactly once** - **Delivery Note first, then invoice (`update_stock=0`):** - With SDBNB off, the Delivery Note books COGS (Dr COGS, Cr Inventory) and the invoice books only receivable, income and tax. - With SDBNB on, the Delivery Note books Dr SDBNB, Cr Inventory. The invoice then reverses Dr COGS, Cr SDBNB. COGS is recognised once, at billing time. - **Invoice with no Delivery Note (`update_stock=1`):** The invoice's own stock ledger entries drive the COGS GL rows, and `validate_delivery_note` blocks mixing this with a Delivery Note. - **Cancellations and returns:** These use the `return_against` and `dn_detail` links, together with `sales_and_purchase_return.py`.

A Sales Invoice linked to a Delivery Note posts only revenue, and optionally a reclass of a holding account. I read the Sales Invoice and Delivery Note code. The Delivery Note and Sales Invoice use it to update the Sales Order's delivered and billed quantities through `update_prevdoc_status`. - The Sales Order posts no stock or GL entries. It only reserves stock and tracks quantities. **2. Delivery Note** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`, class `DeliveryNote`) - On submit it updates the Sales Order status, then calls `update_stock_ledger`. It posts Credit Stock In Hand and Debit the item's expense account, which is COGS. - When the company has `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` set, the Delivery Note item's expense account is the "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" account instead of COGS. `get_item_details.py` and `company.py` look like where this is set up. - `on_cancel` reverses the stock ledger and GL entries. `check_next_docstatus` blocks cancelling a Delivery Note that has a submitted invoice. **3. Sales Invoice** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`, class `SalesInvoice`) - The Delivery Note link is stored in `delivery_note` and `dn_detail` on each Sales Invoice item. - `validate_delivery_note` throws "Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes" if `update_stock` is set on an invoice whose items link to a Delivery Note. The flow has three stages. I read the key functions in each file. I did not open `make_rm_stock_entry` or the SCO's `populate_items_table` and `update_status`, so my notes on those are inferred from names and call sites. ## 1. Send raw materials to the supplier (Stock Entry, "Send to Subcontractor") **Creating the transfer** - `make_rm_stock_entry(...)` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` builds a Stock Entry from a Subcontracting Order (SCO). It can also build one from a Purchase Order. - The SCO form's whitelisted `make_rm_stock_entry` method is a thin wrapper around it. It is the "Material to Supplier" button. - `add_items_in_ste(...)` in the same file adds the RM rows. It links each row back to the order through `sco_rm_detail`. - `get_items_from_subcontract_order(...)` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` is the whitelisted fetch used from the Stock Entry form. It calls `make_rm_stock_entry`. **Validating the transfer** - `StockEntry` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py` sets `subcontract_data` in its setup. That is a dict with `order_doctype`, `order_field` (`subcontracting_order`), `order_supplied_items_field` (`Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`) and `rm_detail_field`. - It dispatches the purpose "Send to Subcontractor" to `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`, defined in `services/subcontracting.py`. - `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry.validate()` runs these checks: - `validate_subcontract_order` - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` - `_get_required_qty_for_bom` - `_validate_transfer_qty` - `_link_rm_detail_if_missing` - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` - `get_total_supplied_qty` - `get_total_returned_qty` - `get_order_rm_detail` - `StockEntry.validate_closed_subcontracting_order` blocks transfers against a closed order. - The stock moves out of the company warehouse to the supplier warehouse through the normal Stock Entry stock-ledger posting. **Tracking against the SCO on submit or cancel** - `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry.on_submit` and `on_cancel` call `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`. That function uses: - `get_supplied_items(...)`, which sums `transfer_qty` from submitted Stock Entries per `rm_detail`. Returns go into `returned_qty`. - `_update_supplied_items_in_order`, which writes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` onto the `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` rows. - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting`, which calls `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting`. - `StockEntry.update_subcontracting_order_status` calls `set_subcontracting_order_status` in `subcontracting_order.py`. This recomputes the SCO's status. - `StockEntry.reserve_stock_for_subcontracting` calls `SubcontractingOrder.reserve_raw_materials`. - `StockEntry.update_wo_reservation_for_subcontracting` releases the Work Order's own reservation for these items. **Returns** - `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` and `get_materials_from_supplier` in `subcontracting_controller.py` handle returning RM from the supplier. ## 2. Subcontracting Order (`SubcontractingOrder`) The class is in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` and extends `SubcontractingController`. - **Building the order:** - `populate_items_table` and `validate_purchase_order_for_subcontracting` build it from a Purchase Order. - `validate_service_items` and `validate_supplied_items` check the order. - `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po` writes back to the Purchase Order. - **Supplied items table:** `SubcontractingController.create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` explodes the BOM into the supplied-items table. It uses these helpers: - `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items` - `_get_materials_from_bom` - `__add_supplied_or_received_item` - `__set_supplied_or_received_items` - `__get_transferred_items` - **Costing the supplied items:** - `update_rate_for_supplied_items` and `set_rate_for_supplied_items` set the RM rate. - `set_valuation_rate_for_rm` is the other costing hook in the controller. - **Totals and bin updates:** - `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` - `calculate_service_costs` - `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount` - `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` - `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` - **Status:** `update_status`, `set_subcontracting_order_status` and `update_subcontracting_order_status` manage it. The per-row received quantity is handled by the Subcontracting Receipt's status updater (`update_status_updater_args`). - **Creating the receipt:** `make_subcontracting_receipt` calls `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt`. It maps SCO items to SCR items and carries the order references over. ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt (`SubcontractingReceipt`) The class is in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py` and also extends `SubcontractingController`. **validate** - `reset_supplied_items` clears the supplied items. - `set_missing_values` calls `set_available_qty_for_consumption` and `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`. - `get_secondary_items` and `validate_secondary_items` handle by-products and scrap. - `validate_accepted_warehouse` and `validate_rejected_warehouse` check the warehouses. - `SubcontractingController.validate` and `before_validate` run `set_items_bom`, `get_available_materials` and `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received`. These use `__get_transferred_items` and `__get_received_items` to take the RM transferred to the supplier. They consume it based on either BOM or material transfer (`__get_backflush_based_on`). They also pick batch and serial numbers (`set_batch_for_supplied_items`, `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle`). **Cost roll-up** (`calculate_items_qty_and_amount`) - Each supplied item's amount is `consumed_qty * rate`. - Those amounts are summed per FG row through `reference_name` into `rm_supp_cost`, and `rm_cost_per_qty` is that cost divided by the received quantity. - Secondary-item (scrap) cost is subtracted through `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - The FG row's `rate` is: - `rm_cost_per_qty` - plus `service_cost_per_qty` - plus `additional_cost_per_qty`, from `calculate_additional_costs` - plus the landed cost voucher share - For BOM-based rows, the amount is also scaled by the BOM's `cost_allocation_per`. - It then sets `total_qty` and `total`. - `get_supplied_items_cost` is the helper that returns the cost of the supplied items for one FG row. **on_submit** - `validate_closed_subcontracting_order` and `validate_bom_required_qty` check the order and BOM quantities. - `update_status_updater_args` and `update_prevdoc_status` update the received quantity on the SCO. - `set_subcontracting_order_status(update_bin=False)` refreshes the SCO status. - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` writes `consumed_qty` back onto the SCO supplied-item rows. It does this through `__update_consumed_materials` and `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`, and the consumed quantity is capped at `supplied_qty`. - `update_stock_ledger` in `subcontracting_controller.py` calls `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty`, which refreshes the order's bin quantities. It then posts these entries: - FG receipt entries with `incoming_rate = rate` and `recalculate_rate = 1` - rejected-warehouse entries - supplier-warehouse entries from `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse`, which deduct the consumed RM - `make_gl_entries` (the SCR's `get_gl_entries` override) posts the GL entries. - The SCR submit then calls `update_status`, `auto_create_purchase_receipt` and `update_job_card`. **on_cancel** reverses the same steps. `reset_raw_materials`, a whitelisted method, rebuilds the supplied items. **Reconciliation across the flow** - `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` holds three counters: `supplied_qty` and `returned_qty` from Stock Entries, and `consumed_qty` from Subcontracting Receipts. - The difference between supplied and consumed is the RM still sitting at the supplier. `get_current_stock` and `get_pending_subcontracted_quantity` use these figures.

final answer
The flow below is traced from the code. I read the receipt, order and stock-entry functions directly. I did not open `make_rm_stock_entry` or the supplied-item rate logic in `SubcontractingController`, so those parts are described from function names and call edges. ## 1. Subcontracting Order: the plan for raw materials - File: `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`, class `SubcontractingOrder`, which extends `SubcontractingController`. - The order has an `items` table (finished goods) and a `supplied_items` table (child doctype Subcontracting Order Supplied Item). - Each supplied-item row carries `required_qty`, `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `consumed_qty`. - `validate` calls `validate_supplied_items` and `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount`. - `before_validate` and `validate` in the controller build the raw-material rows through `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` and `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`. These use the private helpers `__identify_change_in_item_table`, `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` and `__validate_supplied_or_received_items`. The rows come from the BOM, or from the Purchase Order's supplied-items table. - `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` update the Bin. They reserve raw material for subcontracting through `stock_bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting()`. - `update_status` and the module-level `set_subcontracting_order_status` and `update_subcontracting_order_status` compute the order status. The status depends on `per_received` and on the supplied quantities. - `make_subcontracting_receipt` (whitelisted, around line 441) is the mapper that creates a Subcontracting Receipt from the order. ## 2. Transfer to the supplier: Stock Entry "Send to Subcontractor" - `make_rm_stock_entry` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` (around line 1344) builds a Stock Entry from the order's pending raw materials. Tests call it, for example in `test_subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred.py`. - `get_materials_from_supplier` (around line 1537) does the reverse: it returns unused materials from the supplier. - `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` holds the class `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`: - `validate` calls `validate_subcontract_order`. This throws if more is transferred than the order allows. - The check depends on the Buying Settings option `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on`. When it is BOM, `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` and `_get_required_qty_for_bom` apply. When it is "Material Transferred for Subcontract", `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` applies. - Both paths use `_validate_transfer_qty`, `get_total_supplied_qty`, `get_total_returned_qty`, `get_order_rm_detail` and `_link_rm_detail_if_missing`. - `on_submit` and `on_cancel` call `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`. That function runs `_get_order_supplied_items`, `_get_supplied_items_details`, and `get_supplied_items` (which sums `transfer_qty` by item). It then writes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` into the order's supplied-items rows through `_update_supplied_items_in_order`. - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` refreshes the Bin reservation. - `get_items_from_subcontract_order` is the pull-in helper. - `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py`: `MaterialTransferStockEntry.on_submit` and `on_cancel` call `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`, which delegates to `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`. - The stock moves from the company warehouse to the supplier warehouse (`supplier_warehouse`). - The report `erpnext/buying/report/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred.py` (`get_order_items_to_supply`) shows required, transferred and returned quantities for open orders. ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt: consumption, cost roll-up and posting - File: `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`, class `SubcontractingReceipt`, which also extends `SubcontractingController`. Its child tables are `items` and `supplied_items` (Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item, which holds `consumed_qty`, `rate`, `reference_name` and `subcontracting_order`). - `validate`: - `reset_supplied_items` clears and rebuilds the table through the controller's `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received`. The controller's `__get_transferred_items`, `__get_consumed_items`, `__update_consumed_materials` and `get_available_materials` supply transferred and consumed quantities. `set_rate_for_supplied_items` and `__set_consumed_qty` set rates and consumed quantities. - `set_missing_values` calls `set_available_qty_for_consumption` and `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`. - The `set_supplied_items_*` methods fill expense account, cost center and inventory dimensions. - `reset_raw_materials` is the whitelisted method behind the "Reset Raw Materials Table" button in `subcontracting_receipt.js`. - Cost roll-up is in `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`, plus the controller's `calculate_additional_costs` and `get_supplied_items_cost`: - For each supplied-item row, `amount = consumed_qty × rate`. These amounts are summed per finished-good row through `reference_name` into `rm_supp_cost`, and `rm_cost_per_qty = rm_supp_cost / qty`. - The finished-good `rate` is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed-cost-voucher cost per qty`. - Secondary items (by-products and scrap) are costed through `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - If the item has a BOM, `cost_allocation_per` from the BOM scales the amount. - `item.amount` and the document's `total` and `total_qty` are then set. - `calculate_additional_costs` spreads the additional costs over the items, by quantity or by amount. - `validate_bom_required_qty` and `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty` check consumption against the BOM on submit. - `on_submit` runs in this order: 1. `validate_closed_subcontracting_order` 2. `validate_bom_required_qty` 3. `update_status_updater_args` and `update_prevdoc_status`. These update the order's `received_qty` and `per_received`. 4. `set_subcontracting_order_status`, which calls the order's `update_status`. 5. `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`. It uses `__update_consumed_materials` and `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`, which write `consumed_qty` back to the order's supplied-items rows, capped at `supplied_qty`. 6. `update_stock_reservation_entries` 7. `update_stock_ledger` 8. `make_gl_entries` 9. `repost_future_sle_and_gle` 10. `update_status` 11. `auto_create_purchase_receipt` 12. `update_job_card` - `update_stock_ledger` in the controller: - It first calls `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty`, which refreshes the order's Bin quantities. - Finished goods are received into the accepted warehouse at the rolled-up `rate`, with `incoming_rate` and `recalculate_rate`. Rejected quantity goes to `rejected_warehouse`. - `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse` posts negative Stock Ledger Entries for each supplied item. These are `-consumed_qty` in `supplier_warehouse`, linked through `dependant_sle_voucher_detail_no = reference_name`. This is where raw material leaves the supplier's stock. - `get_gl_entries` (around line 703) books the inventory and the "service / raw-material consumed" accounts. The rows use the `expense_account` set in `set_service_expense_account`, `set_expense_account_for_subcontracted_items` and `set_supplied_items_expense_account`. - `on_cancel` reverses the same steps: it calls `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` again, then `update_stock_ledger` and `make_gl_entries_on_cancel`. ## 4. Related paths - Purchase Order services in `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/services/subcontracting.py` (`update_subcontracting_order_status`) and Sales Order services in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/subcontracting.py` (`update_subcontracting_order_status`) sync order status. - `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_inward_controller.py` is the mirror flow, where the customer supplies the raw materials. It is not part of this flow.

final answer
**Flow:** raw materials go out to the supplier on a Send to Subcontractor stock entry. That entry updates the Subcontracting Order's supplied items. The Subcontracting Receipt then consumes those materials and rolls their cost into the finished goods rate. I read the code for the receipt, the order and the stock entry service. I did not read the bodies of most controller functions, so what they do is inferred from their names and call sites. **1. Subcontracting Order (SCO)** - The doctype class is in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`. - It builds on `SubcontractingController` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`. - The order is created from a Purchase Order with the service item and finished goods item. `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po` writes the subcontracted quantity back to the PO. - `set_missing_values` and `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` / `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items` fill the order's `supplied_items` table. The raw materials come from the BOM through `_get_materials_from_bom` and `__add_supplied_or_received_item`. The table is `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`. - `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` maintain the Bin quantities. The finished item is ordered, and the raw materials are reserved at the supplier warehouse. The controller version is `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty`. - `update_status` and the module functions `set_subcontracting_order_status` and `update_subcontracting_order_status` set the status. The receipt side does the same through `SubcontractingController.set_subcontracting_order_status`. **2. Transfer of raw materials to the supplier** - `make_rm_stock_entry` in `subcontracting_controller.py` (line 1344) creates a Material Transfer for Subcontract stock entry from the SCO. It uses the helper `add_items_in_ste` and sets the `sco_rm_detail` link on each row. - `get_items_from_subcontract_order` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` also pulls the items. - The class `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` in that file handles validation: - `validate_subcontract_order` and `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` check the transfer against the order. - `_get_required_qty_for_bom` and `_validate_transfer_qty` limit the quantity to what the order allows. - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` and `_link_rm_detail_if_missing` connect each row to the order's supplied item row. - `get_total_supplied_qty` and `get_total_returned_qty` work out how much has already gone out or come back. - On submit and cancel, `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` runs. It uses `_get_order_supplied_items`, `_get_supplied_items_details` and `_update_supplied_items_in_order` to write the transferred quantity into the SCO's `supplied_qty`. `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` then updates the reserved quantity. - Materials can be sent back with `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` and `get_materials_from_supplier` (line 1537 and line 1489 of the controller). - Reports that show the outstanding transfers are `subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred`, `subcontract_order_summary` and `subcontracted_item_to_be_received`, all under `erpnext/buying/report/`. **3. Subcontracting Receipt (SCR)** - `make_subcontracting_receipt` (line 441 of `subcontracting_order.py`) creates the receipt from the order. The class `SubcontractingReceipt(SubcontractingController)` is in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. - Child tables are `Subcontracting Receipt Item` and `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item`. - The controller works out what is still at the supplier: - `__get_transferred_items` and `__get_received_items` read what was sent and what was received. - `__get_consumed_items` and `__update_consumed_materials` work out what was already consumed. - `get_available_materials` combines these into the available quantity. - `__get_pending_qty_to_receive` gives the quantity still to receive. - The controller then builds `supplied_items` with `__set_supplied_or_received_items` and `__add_supplied_or_received_item`. - `__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer` is used when the order's backflush setting is "Material Transferred for Subcontract". `_get_materials_from_bom` is used for the BOM-based setting. - Rates and batch or serial numbers are set by `set_rate_for_supplied_items`, `update_rate_for_supplied_items`, `set_batch_for_supplied_items`, `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle` and `__set_batch_nos`. - The receipt's `set_available_qty_for_consumption` and `validate_bom_required_qty` check the consumed quantities, and `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty` returns them per raw material. - `SubcontractingReceipt.validate` runs `reset_supplied_items`, then `set_missing_values`, which calls `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`. It then runs `calculate_additional_costs` and `get_current_stock`. **4. Cost roll-up** - `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` in `SubcontractingReceipt` does the roll-up. - For each supplied item, `amount = consumed_qty * rate`. The amounts are summed per receipt item into `rm_supp_cost`, and `rm_cost_per_qty` is that sum divided by `received_qty` (or `qty` if there is no `received_qty`). - Secondary (scrap) item values go into `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. `get_secondary_items` and `validate_secondary_items` handle those rows. - The finished item `rate` is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed cost per qty`. The landed cost term comes from `landed_cost_voucher_amount / qty`. - If the item has a BOM, the amount is scaled by `cost_allocation_per` from the BOM. - `calculate_additional_costs` in the controller handles the additional-cost part. - `get_supplied_items_cost(item_row_id)` returns the raw material cost for one item row. **5. Posting on submit** - `SubcontractingReceipt.on_submit` runs these steps in order: - `validate_closed_subcontracting_order` - `validate_bom_required_qty` - `update_status_updater_args` - `update_prevdoc_status` - `set_subcontracting_order_status` - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`, which calls `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` and writes `consumed_qty` back to the SCO's supplied items - `update_stock_ledger` - `make_gl_entries` - `repost_future_sle_and_gle` - `update_status` - `auto_create_purchase_receipt` - `update_job_card` - `update_stock_ledger` in the controller calls `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse`. That entry takes the consumed raw materials out of the supplier warehouse. The finished goods go into the receipt warehouse, and the SLE rows come from `StockController.make_sl_entries`. - `get_gl_entries` in the receipt, together with the `set_supplied_items_expense_account` and `set_service_expense_account` helpers, handles the accounting. Stock moves from the raw material and finished goods accounts to the service expense account. - `on_cancel` reverses these steps. - `update_status` also updates the receipt's own status.

final answer
The flow has three stages: transfer to the supplier, tracking against the Subcontracting Order, and receipt with cost roll-up. I did not read every function body, so the notes below say which parts are inferred. ## 1. Transfer raw materials to the supplier - **Creating the Stock Entry:** `make_rm_stock_entry()` in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` is whitelisted and builds the Stock Entry. It works for a Subcontracting Order or a Purchase Order. - It maps the order to a Stock Entry with `get_mapped_doc` and sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"`. - It links `subcontracting_order` and sets `sco_rm_detail` (or `po_detail` for a Purchase Order) on each row. - It sets `s_warehouse` to the item's warehouse or reserve warehouse. It sets `t_warehouse` to the order's `supplier_warehouse`. - It skips items that are already fully transferred, using `over_transfer_allowance` from Buying Settings. - `main_item_code` and `subcontracted_item` tie each raw material to its finished good. Serial and batch bundles are carried over. - **Other ways to create it:** `get_items_from_subcontract_order` and `get_supplied_items` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`. Returns go through `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` and `get_materials_from_supplier` in the controller. - **Stock Entry class:** `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py` registers `"Send to Subcontractor": SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`. - **Validation:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` in `services/subcontracting.py` runs these checks: - `validate_subcontract_order` - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` - `_validate_transfer_qty` - `get_total_supplied_qty` - `get_total_returned_qty` - `get_order_rm_detail` ## 2. Tracking against the Subcontracting Order - **On submit and cancel:** `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry.on_submit` and `on_cancel` call `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`, which uses these helpers: - `_get_order_supplied_items` - `_get_supplied_items_details` - `_update_supplied_items_in_order` - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` These update `supplied_qty` on the order's child table, `SubcontractingOrderSuppliedItem`. I did not read the bodies, so that is inferred from the names. - **Status update:** `StockEntry.update_subcontracting_order_status` calls `set_subcontracting_order_status` in `subcontracting_order.py`. That runs `SubcontractingOrder.update_status`, which sets the order's transferred percentage and status. The `per_transferred` field on the Stock Entry also drives this. - **Order-side logic:** - `SubcontractingOrder` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` extends `SubcontractingController`. - `validate_supplied_items` and `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount` check and total the supplied items. - `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` updates the reserved quantity. - `make_subcontracting_receipt` maps the order to a receipt. - **Building the supplied-items list:** The controller's `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` calls `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items`. That in turn calls `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` and `__validate_supplied_or_received_items`. It uses these helpers to work out what is available at the supplier: - `get_available_materials` - `__get_received_items` - `__get_consumed_items` - `__update_consumed_materials` ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt and cost roll-up - **Class:** `SubcontractingReceipt` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. Its child table `SubcontractingReceiptSuppliedItem` holds the consumed raw materials. - **Before validation:** `before_validate` runs these, which set up the BOM, cost center and expense accounts: - `validate_items_qty` - `set_items_bom` - `set_items_cost_center` - `set_service_expense_account` - `set_expense_account_for_subcontracted_items` - **Validation:** - `reset_supplied_items` and `set_missing_values` run first. `set_missing_values` calls `set_available_qty_for_consumption` and `calculate_items_qty_and_amount`. - After those, `set_supplied_items_expense_account`, `set_supplied_items_cost_center` and `set_supplied_items_inventory_dimensions` run. - `validate_secondary_items` and `validate_accepted_warehouse` run at submit. - **Supplied-item valuation in the controller:** - `update_rate_for_supplied_items` and `set_rate_for_supplied_items` set each raw material's rate. They call `get_incoming_rate` on the supplier warehouse with `consumed_qty`. - `__set_consumed_qty`, `__set_batch_nos` and `__set_serial_nos` allocate consumed quantities to batches and serial numbers. - `get_supplied_items_cost` sums `consumed_qty × rate` for one item row. - **Cost roll-up:** `SubcontractingReceipt.calculate_items_qty_and_amount` does this. - For each supplied item it computes `amount = consumed_qty × rate` and sums it per `reference_name`. - For each finished item it sets `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty = rm_supp_cost / (received_qty or qty)`. - It subtracts secondary or scrap item cost through `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - The finished-good rate is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed cost voucher cost per qty`. - When a BOM is set, the amount is scaled by the BOM's `cost_allocation_per`. - Totals are then accumulated. - The controller's `calculate_additional_costs` supplies the additional cost per qty. - **On submit:** `on_submit` runs these in order: - `validate_closed_subcontracting_order` - `validate_bom_required_qty` - `update_status_updater_args` - `update_prevdoc_status` - `set_subcontracting_order_status` - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` - `update_stock_reservation_entries` - `update_stock_ledger` - `make_gl_entries` - `repost_future_sle_and_gle` - `update_status` - `auto_create_purchase_receipt` - `update_job_card` - **Reconciliation back to the order:** - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` calls `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`. That writes `consumed_qty` onto the order's supplied-items rows, capped at `supplied_qty`. - `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty` calls `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` on the order. - `set_subcontracting_order_status` refreshes the order status. - **Stock Ledger:** In the controller, `update_stock_ledger` posts the finished goods into the receiving warehouse, using `item.rate` as the incoming rate. `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse` posts negative entries for each supplied item's `consumed_qty` out of the `supplier_warehouse`. A rejected quantity goes to the rejected warehouse at zero rate. - **GL entries:** `SubcontractingReceipt.get_gl_entries` creates the accounting entries. - **Purchase Receipt and invoice:** For a Purchase Order based flow, `PurchaseReceiptItemSupplied` is the equivalent supplied-items table. Both `PurchaseReceipt` and `PurchaseInvoice` use it.

final answer
The flow has three stages: the raw materials go out to the supplier, the Subcontracting Order records what was sent, and the Subcontracting Receipt consumes it and rolls its cost into the finished goods. I traced this by reading the code. I did not run any of it, and I did not read the bodies of `make_rm_stock_entry`, `get_available_materials`, `set_rate_for_supplied_items` or `reserve_raw_materials`, so their descriptions below come from names and call-graph context. ## 1. Subcontracting Order: demand and the raw-material plan Files: `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` and `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`. - `SubcontractingOrder` extends `SubcontractingController`, which extends `StockController`. - `populate_items_table` builds the service and finished-good items. - The controller's `validate` and `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received("supplied_items")` fill the `supplied_items` table. That table is the "Subcontracting Order Supplied Item" child table, with `required_qty`, `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `consumed_qty` per raw material. - `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items` calls `__identify_change_in_item_table`, `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` and `__validate_supplied_or_received_items`. - `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` gets raw materials either from the BOM (`_get_materials_from_bom`) or from what was transferred (`__get_transferred_items`, `__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer`). - Which source is used depends on the Buying Settings option `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on`: "BOM" or "Material Transferred for Subcontract". - The controller also handles batch and serial numbers (`__set_batch_nos`, `__set_serial_nos`, `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle`) and alternative items. - `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` update the Bin quantities. The latter reserves raw material stock at the supplier warehouse. - `reserve_raw_materials`, `has_unreserved_stock` and `cancel_stock_reservation_entries` handle stock reservation. - `update_status` and `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po` keep the order status and the linked Purchase Order in step. ## 2. Transfer to the supplier: Stock Entry "Send to Subcontractor" - `make_rm_stock_entry` in `subcontracting_controller.py` builds the Stock Entry from an order. It uses `add_items_in_ste` and fills `sco_rm_detail`, which links each row back to the order's supplied-item row. - The Stock Entry moves stock from the company warehouse to the supplier warehouse (reserve warehouse). - `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` validates the transfer: - `validate_subcontract_order` branches on the backflush setting. - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` uses `_get_required_qty_for_bom`, applies the `over_transfer_allowance` setting, and calls `_validate_transfer_qty`. - `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` requires `subcontracted_item` on each row. - `get_total_supplied_qty` and `get_total_returned_qty` query Stock Entries by `sco_rm_detail`. - `_link_rm_detail_if_missing` and `get_order_rm_detail` link each row to the order's raw-material row. - `MaterialTransferStockEntry` in `stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/material_transfer.py` calls `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` on submit and cancel. - `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry.update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` recalculates `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` on the order's supplied-items rows. - `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` returns surplus material from the supplier. It is called from `get_materials_from_supplier`, which is also in `subcontracting_controller.py`. - The report `buying/report/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred` (`get_order_items_to_supply`) shows required versus transferred quantities. ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt: consumption and cost roll-up Order to receipt: `make_subcontracting_receipt` and `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt` in `subcontracting_order.py`. `SubcontractingReceipt` is in `subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. **Validate:** - `reset_supplied_items` and `reset_raw_materials` call `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received`. - `get_available_materials` and `set_available_qty_for_consumption` work out what is available at the supplier. - `set_rate_for_supplied_items`, `update_rate_for_supplied_items` and `set_valuation_rate_for_rm` set the raw-material rates. These are valued from the supplier-warehouse stock, which comes from the transfer Stock Entries. - `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` does the cost roll-up: - Each supplied item's `amount` is `consumed_qty × rate`. - That amount is summed per finished-good row through `reference_name`, giving `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty` (divided by `received_qty` or `qty`). - Secondary-item cost is netted off through `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - The finished item's `rate` is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed-cost-voucher cost per qty`. - If the row has a BOM, the amount is scaled by the BOM's `cost_allocation_per`. - It then totals quantity and amount. - `calculate_additional_costs` and `get_supplied_items_cost` support this. `get_secondary_items` handles scrap and co-products. - `validate_bom_required_qty`, `validate_accepted_warehouse` and `validate_rejected_warehouse` check the receipt. **On submit (`on_submit`):** - `validate_closed_subcontracting_order`. - `validate_bom_required_qty`. - `update_status_updater_args` and `update_prevdoc_status` update `received_qty` and `per_received` on the order. - `set_subcontracting_order_status`. - `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`, which uses `__update_consumed_materials`, `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` and `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty`. It writes `consumed_qty` back to the order's supplied rows, capped at `supplied_qty`. - `update_stock_ledger` in the controller: - It calls `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty`, which updates the Bin quantities. - Finished goods are received into the warehouse at the rolled-up `rate`, with `recalculate_rate`. Rejected quantity goes to the rejected warehouse. - `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse` posts negative `consumed_qty` for each raw material from `supplier_warehouse`. This removes the supplier's stock. - `make_gl_entries` and `get_gl_entries` post the accounting entries, followed by `repost_future_sle_and_gle` and `update_job_card`. - `auto_create_purchase_receipt` can then create a Purchase Receipt. **Cancel:** `on_cancel` reverses these steps through the same functions.

final answer
The flow has three stages. The outbound transfer and the Subcontracting Order tracking are shown directly in the code I read. I did not read `make_rm_stock_entry`, `get_supplied_items` or the Stock Entry dispatch code, so what I say about them comes from names and call sites. ## 1. Subcontracting Order (SCO) defines what must be supplied - `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` holds the `SubcontractingOrder` class. It inherits `SubcontractingController`. - Its `supplied_items` table is the "Subcontracting Order Supplied Item" child table. It stores `rm_item_code`, `required_qty`, `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty`, `total_supplied_qty`, `consumed_qty` and `reserve_warehouse`. - Rows are built by `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received` → `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items`. Those call the private helpers `__identify_change_in_item_table`, `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` and `__validate_supplied_or_received_items`. All of this is in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`. - The helper `__add_supplied_or_received_item` builds each row, using BOM quantities or quantities already transferred. - `reserve_raw_materials` creates a `StockReservation` for the supplied items when `reserve_stock` is set. - `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` and `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` update the Bin. - `update_status` and `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po` keep the SCO and its Purchase Order status in sync. ## 2. Sending raw materials to the supplier - `make_rm_stock_entry` in `subcontracting_controller.py` builds the "Send to Subcontractor" Stock Entry from the SCO. `get_materials_from_supplier` and `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` handle returns of unused material. - The Stock Entry validates in `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`): - `validate` calls `validate_subcontract_order`. - That method reads the Buying Settings option `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on` and checks the transfer against the SCO. - In BOM mode it uses `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom`, `_get_required_qty_for_bom` and `_validate_transfer_qty`. These enforce the required quantity plus `over_transfer_allowance`, net of returned quantity. - In "Material Transferred for Subcontract" mode it uses `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer`. - `_link_rm_detail_if_missing` links each Stock Entry row to the SCO supplied-item row. - `MaterialTransferStockEntry` (`services/material_transfer.py`) calls `update_transferred_qty` and `update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` in `on_submit` and `on_cancel`. - `SendToSubcontractorStockEntry.update_subcontract_order_supplied_items` does the tracking: - `_get_order_supplied_items` and `_get_supplied_items_details` (which calls `get_supplied_items`) collect the quantities. - `_update_supplied_items_in_order` writes `supplied_qty`, `returned_qty` and `total_supplied_qty` onto the SCO supplied-item rows. - `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` calls `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting`. - `Stock Entry.update_subcontracting_order_status` in `stock_entry.py` refreshes the SCO status. - The report `subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred.py` shows required, transferred and returned quantities per SCO through `get_order_items_to_supply`. ## 3. Subcontracting Receipt (SCR) consumes the materials and rolls up cost - `make_subcontracting_receipt` in `subcontracting_order.py` creates the SCR from the SCO. - `SubcontractingReceipt` is in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. It also inherits `SubcontractingController`. - Consumption rows: - `reset_raw_materials` clears `supplied_items` and calls `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received`. - `get_available_materials` and `__get_transferred_items` use the transferred quantities, and `__get_received_items` and `__get_consumed_items` use what the supplier has already received and consumed. - `__update_consumed_materials` totals consumed quantities, and `__set_consumed_qty` and `__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer` set the consumed quantity per row. - `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle`, `__set_batch_nos` and `__set_serial_nos` copy serial and batch data to the consumed rows. - `set_available_qty_for_consumption` computes `available_qty_for_consumption` as `total_supplied_qty - consumed_qty` from the SCO supplied items. - Rates and cost roll-up: - `update_rate_for_supplied_items` and `set_rate_for_supplied_items` set each raw-material `rate` from `get_incoming_rate`, using the supplier warehouse. - `reset_supplied_items` clears the table or re-rates it, depending on the backflush setting. - `calculate_additional_costs` (controller) distributes additional costs by Amount or Qty into `additional_cost_per_qty`. - `SubcontractingReceipt.calculate_items_qty_and_amount` does the roll-up: - Each supplied row gets `amount = consumed_qty * rate`, summed per finished-good row into `rm_supp_cost` and `rm_cost_per_qty`. - `get_secondary_items` and `remove_secondary_items` add secondary or scrap items, which feed `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`. - The finished-good `rate` is `rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + landed-cost-voucher cost per qty`. - When a BOM is set, `amount` is scaled by the BOM's `cost_allocation_per`. - The method then sets `total_qty` and `total`. - `get_supplied_items_cost` returns the raw-material cost for one row. - `set_missing_values` runs `set_available_qty_for_consumption`, `calculate_additional_costs` and `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` in order. - I've read the main code paths and I'm now writing up the answer. ## 1. Redistributing charges across Purchase Receipt items This happens in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`, in the `LandedCostVoucher` class. - **Getting the items.** `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` pulls the line items of the chosen receipts into the `items` table (`Landed Cost Item`). It uses the module helper `get_pr_items()`. - **Total charges.** `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` sets `total_taxes_and_charges` to the sum of `base_amount` over the `taxes` table. That table holds the freight and customs rows. - **Per-item split.** `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` does the split unless `distribute_charges_based_on` is "Distribute Manually". - The basis field is Qty, Amount or similar, and it is read through `frappe.scrub(distribute_charges_based_on)`. - Each row gets `applicable_charges = item.<basis> * total_taxes_and_charges / sum(<basis>)`. - Any rounding difference is added to the last row. - It throws an error if the basis totals zero. - **Check on submit.** `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` confirms the per-item charges add up to `total_taxes_and_charges`. This is the check that matters for manual distribution. ## 2. Retroactively updating already-submitted receipts On submit or cancel, `on_submit()` and `on_cancel()` both call `update_landed_cost()`. That method rewrites the existing receipts rather than creating new ones. **Step 1: update the item rows.** For each row in `purchase_receipts`: - It loads the receipt document with `frappe.get_doc`. - `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` sums `applicable_charges` from all submitted (`docstatus=1`) `Landed Cost Item` rows that match each receipt item. The match is on `purchase_receipt_item`, or `stock_entry_item` for a Stock Entry. The sum is written to `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount`. Because it sums across all submitted LCVs, cancelling a voucher removes its share. - `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` is in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`. It recomputes the rate as `(base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom`. - Subcontracting Receipts call `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` instead. - `item.db_update()` saves the new values straight to the database without re-submitting. - `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` refreshes the serial number rates. **Step 2: reverse and re-post stock and GL.** For each receipt: - It sets `docstatus = 2`, then calls `update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` and `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`. This reverses the old Stock Ledger and GL entries. - It sets `docstatus = 1` and calls `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`. Then `update_stock_ledger(...)` posts the stock ledger again, now at the new valuation rate. - It posts GL again with `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` for a Purchase Receipt, or plain `make_gl_entries()` for the other types. - `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` then reposts later stock ledger and GL entries so downstream valuation is corrected. This is in `stock_controller.py` and goes through `StockLedgerService`. **GL composition.** `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()` is called from `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries()`. It uses `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` from the LCV module. That function reads every submitted LCV for the receipt and builds a per-item, per-`expense_account` amount map. The landed cost is then credited to the LCV expense accounts, which are usually "Expenses Included In Valuation", and debited to stock. I did not open the GL composer file itself, so its exact path and internals are unverified. The call chain above comes from the imports and call sites.

I've traced the whole flow, so here's the answer. ## Distributing charges across items **File:** `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`, class `LandedCostVoucher`. - `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` (via `get_pr_items`) copies the line items of each listed receipt into the voucher's `items` table. Each row stores `purchase_receipt_item` (or `stock_entry_item`), `qty`, `amount` and `receipt_document`. - `validate()` calls `set_total_taxes_and_charges()`, which sums the `base_amount` of the `taxes` rows (freight, customs and so on). It then calls `set_applicable_charges_on_item()`. - `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` splits the total across items: - **Basis:** the "Distribute Charges Based On" field, which is Qty or Amount. For "Distribute Manually" the user enters the charges and this step is skipped. - **Formula:** `item.applicable_charges = item.<qty|amount> × total_taxes_and_charges / Σ(basis)`. - **Rounding:** each share is rounded, and any leftover difference is added to the last item. - On submit, `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` checks that the applicable charges add up to the total. A rounding difference within tolerance is absorbed by the last row. Anything larger raises an error. ## Retroactively updating already-submitted receipts `on_submit()` and `on_cancel()` both call `update_landed_cost()`. This is where the existing receipts are changed. 1. **Per-item charge:** `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` sums `Landed Cost Item.applicable_charges` from all submitted voucher rows pointing at each receipt item. It writes the total to `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount`. On cancel, the cancelled voucher is no longer counted, so the amount reverses. 2. **Valuation rate:** `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py` recomputes `item.valuation_rate`. The formula is `(base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / (qty × conversion_factor)`. 3. **Persist:** `item.db_update()` saves the new values to the submitted document without a full save. For non-asset items, `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` also updates `Serial No.purchase_rate`. 4. **Rebuild the ledgers:** for each receipt, the voucher temporarily sets `docstatus = 2` and calls these in order: - `update_stock_ledger(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` - `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` It then sets `docstatus = 1` and calls these in order: - `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(...)` - `update_stock_ledger(...)`, which re-posts Stock Ledger Entries at the new valuation rate - `make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` for a Purchase Receipt - `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` The last call propagates the changed valuation to later transactions. ## GL entries `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` in `landed_cost_voucher.py` builds a map of `(item_code, row name)` → expense account → amount. It finds the submitted vouchers via `Landed Cost Purchase Receipt`. It then splits each tax row's `amount` and `base_amount` per item using the same basis ratio. `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` uses that map: - The stock-in-hand debit includes `landed_cost_voucher_amount`. - `make_landed_cost_gl_entries()` credits each landed-cost expense account (for example, "Expenses Included in Valuation"). The Purchase Invoice, Stock Entry and Subcontracting Receipt composers follow the same pattern.

final answer
A Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) splits its charges across items in `LandedCostVoucher.set_applicable_charges_on_item`. On submit, `update_landed_cost` then recomputes the valuation rate of each linked receipt and reposts its stock and GL entries. I read the LCV, buying-controller and stock-controller code, but I did not open `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer` or `StockLedgerService`. What they do with the LCV flag is inferred from the call chain. ## 1. Distributing charges across items This is in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`, class `LandedCostVoucher`. - **Item list:** `get_items_from_purchase_receipts` fills the LCV's `items` table from the chosen receipts, using the module function `get_pr_items`. Each row is a `Landed Cost Item` carrying `purchase_receipt_item`, `qty`, `amount` and so on. - **Total charges:** `set_total_taxes_and_charges` sets `total_taxes_and_charges` to the sum of `base_amount` over the charge rows (`Landed Cost Taxes and Charges`). - **Proportional split:** `set_applicable_charges_on_item` runs when the distribution method is not "Distribute Manually". - The method is the `distribute_charges_based_on` field, such as Qty, Amount or Distribute Manually. It is turned into a field name with `frappe.scrub`. - Each item gets `applicable_charges = item[field] * total_taxes_and_charges / sum(field over all items)`, rounded to the field's precision. - Any rounding difference is added to the last item. - It throws an error if the total basis is zero. - **Manual mode:** the user enters `applicable_charges` per row. - **Check on submit:** `validate_applicable_charges_for_item` confirms the per-item charges add up to `total_taxes_and_charges`, within a rounding tolerance. `on_submit` calls it first. - **Per-account split for GL:** `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` repeats the proportional split for each charge row's `expense_account`. It returns a map of `(item_code, purchase_receipt_item)` → account → amount and base_amount, which the receipt's GL entry code uses. ## 2. Retroactively updating already-submitted receipts This is `LandedCostVoucher.update_landed_cost`, called from `on_submit` and `on_cancel`. On cancel, the same recomputation drops the cancelled voucher's charges. It runs in two passes over `self.purchase_receipts`. **Pass 1: recompute valuation on the receipt's items.** 1. It loads each receipt with `frappe.get_doc(receipt_document_type, receipt_document)`. 2. `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` sets each item's `landed_cost_voucher_amount`.
